title: Blue Spring
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A one-volume anthology of short stories about delinquents at a run-down boys' high school with indifferent teachers; in the best-known story, Kujo becomes gang leader and must keep defending his place through a dangerous rooftop game (VIZ blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates; Manga Critic review). The boys skip class, fight, commit petty crime and drift toward an adulthood without clear escape (review). Taiyo Matsumoto's 1993 seinen collection, adapted as a live-action film; VIZ rated it Mature (18+) per the review.
life_message: It offers no easy answer, presenting youth as a 'blue time' of anger and emptiness to be lived through honestly (review).

content.note: Gang fights and bullying treated as routine (review); AniList Gangs, Yakuza, Guns; MangaUpdates Gun/s.
'Dark and intense drama' (VIZ blurb); 'violence and despair' (review).

Dangerous rooftop game for gang rank (VIZ blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates); truancy and delinquency (review).

dominant: Adolescent alienation, gang rank by daring, emptiness and violence

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Boys 'answer to reason with their fists' (review); rank defended by dares (blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Truancy, indifferent teachers, no rules followed (review).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Gang peers matter more than family or school.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No faith or custom guides the boys.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Little future; getting through each day (review).

folkways.japan: It reflects 1990s Japanese delinquent (furyo) culture and senpai-kohai gang hierarchy in low-ranked high schools.

delivery.evidence: Review: 'offers no easy answers' and no 'false hope'; digressions and daydreams rather than lessons.
delivery.note: Moods and images carry the stories, and the book argues no position.

winners_losers: No one clearly wins; the boys' anger and drift get sympathy without approval or judgment.
